subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the current single wall-clock chat/agent run deadline with activity-aware idle timeout plus an absolute max-run cap, and how should that map onto existing `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`?
rationale: The remaining work changes core timeout semantics, may add or reinterpret configuration, and affects resource-safety expectations across gateway and embedded-runner paths.

options.title: Define idle plus hard cap
options.body: Choose an idle-vs-absolute-cap contract first, then review or request a focused implementation that keeps safety and user-visible timeout reporting together.

options.title: Land narrow mitigations only
options.body: Review the timeout-notice and subagent-heartbeat PRs independently while leaving this issue open for the broader run-budget contract.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Treat the current 48-hour default plus explicit timeout overrides as sufficient and narrow this issue to timeout messaging or documentation only.

recommendation.title: Define idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Choose an idle-vs-absolute-cap contract first, then review or request a focused implementation that keeps safety and user-visible timeout reporting together.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing owner for a cross-cutting gateway, timeout-defaults, and config-policy decision.
